lines: NAACP Clean Air Act 소송(Southaven 가스터빈 → Colossus 2 전력): 10/30 연방지법이 xAI(SpaceXAI) 기각 신청 기각 — '이동 오염원' 아님·원고적격 인정·시민소송 합헌. 10/19 법무부 기각 신청도 기각(개입만 허용). 본안·예비금지명령(5/6) 미판정. 회사는 10-Q 에 이미 공시 — 판단층이 법적 절차 주석을 안 읽었던 공백 기록

확률 25/50/25 · 가치 $32 · 이정표 29개 변화 없음(기준가 $136.37, 11/2 +1.2% → AI 내재가치 $1,310십억). T9(Boost/EchoStar 거래 확인점)·T10(Colossus 터빈 소송 — 예비금지명령·MDEQ 허가) 신설, 확인점 12/01. 10년물 4.94%(10/30) 다음 월간 입력

Fitch 10/28 BBB+ 불변 — $400억 리스는 1차 레버리지 지표 제외, 레버리지 2027 약 1.0배 전망(금리·체결 8-K 는 여전히 없음, T5 2027-01-07). 10월호 정정: 12/8 락업 '약 40%' → 424B4 원문 최대 7억 9,760만주(5.9%), 10/22 13억주 이미 해제, 2027 연장 락업 17억 6,000만주

sections.html:
• Reference date: 2026-11-03 (KST) · round id 2026-11-03-event · mode event (incremental) · previous round 2026-11 (round 8, monthly) · previous monthly round 2026-11 (Source: round information injected by workflow · _probe/context.json)
  • Reason: The news monitor detected two clusters of reports on 2026-11-03 and launched this round — ① "Federal Court Refuses to Dismiss NAACP Lawsuit Against Elon Musk's SpaceX" (democracy now! · tom's hardware · truthout) ② "SpaceX is in talks to acquire or lease the Boost Mobile network to challenge U.S. carriers" (gsmarena · kucoin). Neither is linked to an existing trigger (trigger_id: null) — reports are not grounds for judgment but items to verify (Source: data/spacex_watch.json due news:naacp-xai-lawsuit:2026-11-03 · news:boost-mobile-talks:2026-11-03, 2026-11-03 16:30 KST)
  • Reference share price: $136.37 — close on 2026-11-02 (Mon), +1.22% from the previous day, volume 91.12 million shares. +1.2% versus the previous round's reference price of $134.72 (10/30) (formula: 136.37 ÷ 134.72 − 1) (stockanalysis daily history, accessed 2026-11-03: latest row 11/2)
  • Scope: Only what the two events touch — event ① covers Axis C (Colossus 2 power → nameplate GW, background of milestone C-2027-1) and Axis E (regulation and litigation); event ② covers Axis A (background of milestone A-2028-1 · the 'U.S. big three mobile carriers' row of the competition timetable). Triggers T9 and T10 are newly created. Axes B and D, probabilities and fair-value recalculation are not performed (Source: prompts/monthly_run.md · state.triggers_next_12m).
Conclusion first: ① It is true — on 2026-10-30 (Fri), the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Mississippi denied the motion to dismiss filed by xAI (now SpaceXAI) and MZX Tech. The court held that the Southaven gas turbine power plant is not a 'nonroad/mobile source' under Mississippi's State Implementation Plan (SIP) and is therefore not exempt from permitting, that the NAACP has statutory standing under the Clean Air Act, and that the citizen-suit provision does not violate Article II of the Constitution or the nondelegation principle. Ten days earlier, on 10/19, the Department of Justice's (U.S. government's) motion to dismiss was also denied (intervention was permitted). This is not a ruling on the merits, and the NAACP's motion for a preliminary injunction (5/6) is still undecided — this is the only path that reaches Colossus 2's power, i.e. the Axis C nameplate GW. The company already disclosed this lawsuit in the legal proceedings note of its 10-Q (10/22) (the lawsuit itself is not a new event — the judgment layer simply had not read that note). ② It is at the report stage — the Washington Post (11/2, also reported by Reuters) said SpaceX is in preliminary talks with EchoStar on acquiring or gaining network access to Boost Mobile, and that it sounded out Verizon, AT&T and T-Mobile about buying network capacity and was turned down by all of them. Neither SpaceX nor EchoStar has issued an 8-K or statement (SpaceX's latest EDGAR filing is the 10/26 8-K; EchoStar's latest is the 10/2 8-K on the conclusion of the DISH DBS restructuring). Therefore no change to the judgments on the 29 milestones · no rules triggered · probabilities 25/50/25 · probability-weighted $32 unchanged. What changed is two triggers (T9 Boost/EchoStar deal checkpoint · T10 Colossus turbine lawsuit checkpoint) and the background facts of Axes A and C (Source: Sections 1–5 below).

sections.title: 1 Case ① — NAACP v. X.AI Corp.: Reporting vs. Original Text vs. Filings
sections.html:
Date (US)FactSource grade · source
2026-02NAACP, 60-day notice of intent to sue⑥ (plaintiffs' counsel) SELC 2026-04-14
2026-04-14Lawsuit filed — plaintiffs NAACP and the NAACP Mississippi State Conference, defendants X.AI Corp. and MZX Tech LLC, U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Mississippi. Allegation: 27 gas turbines at the Southaven (Mississippi) power plant operated without an air permit (2025-08 to 12) — supplying power to Colossus 2 (South Memphis). Claims: declaration of violation · halt of unpermitted turbine operation · installation of best available control technology (BACT) · daily fines. Potential emissions (SELC estimate): NOx over 1,700 tons/year, particulate matter up to 180 tons, CO up to 500 tons, formaldehyde up to 19 tons① (company filing) 10-Q R25 Legal Proceedings, 2026-10-22 · ⑥ SELC 4/14 · ⑤ CNBC 10/31 · Complaint posted by Earthjustice (PDF — body text not read with this round's tools)
2026-05-06NAACP moves for a preliminary injunction (halt turbine operation) — opposed by SpaceXAI; Mississippi state government files an opposing brief (amicus)① 10-Q R25
2026-06SpaceXAI files a motion to dismiss (① turbines are 'nonroad/mobile sources' and exempt from permitting ② NAACP lacks standing ③ citizen-suit provision is unconstitutional). On the 16th of the same month the Department of Justice (U.S. government) intervenes and moves to dismiss — "threat to national security, the economy and energy security," with a statement from the Department of Defense CDAO attached. Per NAACP court filings, 57 turbines (up from 27 in February)⑤ CNBC 10/31 · ⑥ Mississippi Free Press 6/16 · ⑥ Earthjustice 10/20
2026-10-19Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals: denies DOJ's motion to stay the district court proceedings (premature). District court: allows U.S. government intervention but does not recognize authority to dismiss ("cannot unilaterally end a citizen suit")① 10-Q R25 (records appellate denial, permitted intervention, denied dismissal) · ⑥ Earthjustice 10/20 · ⑥ DeSoto County News 10/20
2026-10-30SpaceXAI's motion to dismiss denied — holdings: ⓐ the power plant (Plant) is not a 'nonroad/mobile source' under federal regulations, so it "was not and is not exempt from permit requirements" ⓑ plaintiffs have statutory standing under the Clean Air Act ⓒ citizen-suit plaintiffs sue "in their own name and for themselves," so this is not an exercise of federal executive power (no violation of Article II or private nondelegation). The court acknowledged that the Mississippi Department of Environmental Quality (MDEQ) notified in 2025-07 that 'trailer-mounted, under 12 months = mobile/temporary' is exempt, but held that it is not bound by that interpretation. The merits (whether a violation occurred) and the preliminary injunction are undecided⑥ (plaintiffs) Earthjustice 10/30 · SELC 10/30 · ⑤ CNBC 10/31 · ⑥ TechCrunch 10/31 · The Next Web 11/01 · Order text posted by Earthjustice (PDF — body text not read with this round's tools)
2026-11-032 clusters of reports detected (democracy now! etc.) — reprints of the 10/30 ruling above. Detected on day 4 after the rulingdata/spacex_watch.json due
FilingsNo SpaceX 8-K or IR (latest EDGAR 8-K is 10/26, GPU lease). Company position: no response to CNBC and TechCrunch requests for comment. 10-Q litigation reserve $350M (2026-09-30, all cases combined — not broken out by case)① EDGAR filing list, retrieved 2026-11-03 · 10-Q R83

Differences between sources (recorded): ⓐ Turbine count — complaint 27 (2026-04) / NAACP June filing 57 / Earthjustice and SELC October materials "dozens" / reporting "at least 35" (citing SELC) — because the timing differs, this is read as a record of expansion, not a contradiction ⓑ Potential emissions — SELC 4/14 'NOx over 1,700 tons/year' vs Earthjustice and SELC October 'NOx 5,000 tons, PM 400 tons, formaldehyde 47 tons exceeded' — appears to be a recalculation due to the increased turbine count, but the original calculation is unverified ⓒ MDEQ permit — DeSoto County News "2026-03 permit for 27 turbines" vs Mississippi Free Press "2026-03 permit for 41 permanent turbines" vs SELC 4/14 "separate 41-unit power plant permit under review" — MDEQ permit original text unverified, numbers not adopted ⓓ Case number — complaint header 3:26-cv-00074 (judge initials MPM-JMV) vs judge Debra M. Brown in reporting — reassignment unverified (Sources: table above · Bloomberg Law 4/14 (search summary)).

Confirmed as fact (company filing + plaintiffs' announcements + cross-check with top-grade reporting): ① The suit was filed on 2026-04-14 and the company disclosed it in its 10-Q ② On 10/19 the DOJ motion to dismiss was denied and intervention allowed; the appellate stay was denied ③ On 10/30 the defendants' motion to dismiss was denied ④ The preliminary injunction is undecided. Unconfirmed: full text of the order (PDF not read — holding sentences are quoted from plaintiffs and reporting), the number of turbines covered by the MDEQ permit and its issue date, the number of turbines currently operating, case number and presiding judge (Source: table above).

Whether the outcome of the environmental lawsuit (preliminary injunction, merits) actually changes the nameplate GW expansion schedule can be judged from the GW figures in 4Q26 and 1Q27 earnings (C-2027-1), so it is counted as a milestone without a separate rule (source: state.rule_proposals_not_applied · state.milestones[C-2027-1]).

Expected date: because the report describes 'preliminary talks', no date is estimated — the checkpoints are the next monthly issue 2026-12-01 (KST) and the 10-K (estimated 2027-02). The name prefix does not use 'financing, contract, earnings, Starship' (source: table in Section 2 · scripts/spacex_watch.py trigger_kind).
  • T10 newly added — "Colossus gas turbine Clean Air Act lawsuit — preliminary injunction, interlocutory appeal, and MDEQ permit checkpoints": ① ruling on the preliminary injunction (motion filed 5/6) — an order to halt operations would directly affect Colossus 2 power and nameplate GW ② SpaceXAI interlocutory appeal (§1292(b)) or filing of an answer ③ MDEQ permanent turbine permit text (number covered and issue date — 27 vs 41 unconfirmed) ④ 4Q26 10-K legal proceedings note (changes in reserve by case, risk factors) ⑤ additional filings by the U.S. government (intervening party). Expected date: court schedule not public — checkpoint 2026-12-01 (monthly) → 10-K. Measurement-layer share: court records (PACER/CourtListener) are not the source for any of the four monitors (source: table in Section 1 · 10-Q R25).
  • T3, T4, T5, T7, T8: no change — T7 ⓓ (11/5) and ⓔ (11/6) and T8 ② (deposit 11/4 · acceptance 11/5) have not yet arrived as of this issue (KST 11/3 = U.S. 11/2). The T8 check states explicitly 'Boost/EchoStar terrestrial network deal goes to T9' (source: state.triggers_next_12m).
